fair_value_reason: model_engine reconciled set (deep-modeling round (playbook.json), clean citation audit); supervisor narrative 118.49
supervisor_summary: Reconciled fair value $84.31, against the forecasters' $82.45-119.21 (mean $95.09) after the citation-gate fixes. It uses Kilian's three legs on 13.16B economic shares: 10x NTM EBITDA $112.88, SOTP $55.95 (compute fleet run off at spot, Starlink DCF, Space tree) and 17x P/E $83.91. I opened the 424B4 terms that agents 1 and 3 could not: the restricted shares, the 90-day lease notice and EchoStar, which adds $3.0B of loans. The 10x neocloud multiple behind round 1's 12x / 18x is a September 2025 Loop target; the gate then required one basis, and on trailing filing multiples (MU 8.7x / 11.6x, ORCL 20.3x, megacaps 16.2x) the legs are 10x / 17x (11x / 16x gave $88.12). Agent 1's $119 rests on a 65% external share that overshoots the Q1-27 guide. The base case is 9 GW at YE27 (unit pace at Rubin wattage) and ~$50/W-yr to Q3-27, fading to $18.5 by 2032. Holding pricing into 2029 or reaching 13 GW each add ~24%; a 2028 collapse takes 43% off. The ladder stays near the forecasters' (median ~$120), with five judgment calls for Kilian.
key_drivers: Compute rental price durability: new deals at ~$50+/W-yr (CFO) vs an $18.5/W-yr NPV-0 price and ~$24-33/W-yr on the Anthropic contract. Holding into 2029 is +24% FV; a 2028 collapse to break-even is -43%.

Horizon multiple on peak-pricing EBITDA: 10x / 17x on one trailing filing basis (MU 8.7x / 11.6x, ORCL 20.3x P/E, META and AMZN 16.2x) gives $84; the pre-gate 11x / 16x $88; 12x / 18x $95; Kilian's 15x / 27x $118.
Year-end 2027 capacity: 200-220k GPUs a month turning to Rubin (2.64 kW vs 1.94 kW per GPU) gives ~9 GW, vs Musk's 13 GW (+24%, but net debt ~$162B at the horizon).
How much of the fleet is rented out: 55% / 50% fits the Q1-27 guide; agent 1's 65% / 55% adds 14% to fair value but overshoots the guide.
Economic share count: the 1,302M Musk restricted shares need a Mars colony or 100 TW/yr of non-Earth compute (424B4), so per-share value is ~9% above the headline count.
